title: Standard Library
body:
Code that ships with [[Python]] and is one `import` away. "Batteries included" is the slogan and
it is most of why a first course can draw pictures in week three.

```python
import math
import random

math.sqrt(16)            # 4.0
math.pi                  # 3.14159...
random.randint(1, 6)     # a die roll
random.choice(colours)   # pick one
```

The three this course uses:

| Module | For |
|---|---|
| `math` | `sqrt`, `pi`, `floor`, `ceil`, trig. The equivalent of C's `cmath`, see [[Library]] |
| `random` | dice, shuffling, sampling, test data |
| `turtle` | drawing by moving a pen: `forward`, `left`, `penup`. Loops become visible |

**`random` is not random.** It is a seeded pseudo-random generator: same seed, same sequence,
every time. `Books/`'s [[Random Numbers]] has the full argument, and the practical consequence
matters here rather than later, because `random.seed(42)` is what makes a program with dice in it
testable at all. See [[Test Coverage]].

**`turtle` is worth more than it looks.** Drawing a square is four lines of duplicated code until
you write a [[While loop|loop]], and drawing a spiral is impossible without one, so it turns
[[Repetition]] into something you can see going wrong. The same trick is why
[[Recursion]] is usually first shown as a tree or a snowflake.

Importing is also the first time a program is made of more than one file, which is where
[[INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTER SCIENCE 2]] picks up with [[Header File]] and separate compilation.
